sourceQuestions.sourceText: Circle the bossy verb in each instruction. a Pick up your toothbrush. b Put toothpaste on it. c Spit out the toothpaste.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: a Pick (up) • b Put • c Spit (out)

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Write a or an. apple party egg sweet orange present
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: an apple • a party • an egg • a sweet • an orange • a present

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Number the steps 1 to 4 in the right order. Drink it! Get a cup. Add a straw. Pour the juice.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Get a cup 1 • Pour the juice 2 • Add a straw 3 • Drink it! 4

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Write a ly word to say how. Choose from: carefully quietly. a ___ carry the glass of water. b ___ close the door. The baby is asleep.
Which ones are instructions? Tick them. a Wash your hands. b The cat is black. c Shut the door. d I like cake.
Add the time words First, Next, Then, Finally to cross the road safely. find a safe place to cross. stand near the kerb. look both ways. cross when nothing is coming.
Write a bossy verb to start each instruction. ___ the ball. ___ up your coat. ___ the door.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: For example: Kick / Throw the ball • Hang up your coat • Shut / Open the door

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Write three numbered instructions for washing your hands.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Three numbered steps in order, each starting with a bossy verb — e.g. 1 Wet your hands. 2 Rub on soap. 3 Rinse and dry your hands.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: In "Mix the eggs", the word Mix is a ( noun ) ( bossy verb ) ( time word )
We write an before ( egg ) ( cake ) ( tin )
The list of things you need is called ( Dear Diary ) ( The End ) ( You will need )
Instructions must be in the ( right order ) ( wrong order ) ( any order )
The word slowly tells us ( where to do it ) ( how to do it ) ( who does it )
